question: At the existing fixed-cutoff MLSE baseline (cutoff 2.0 s after each trial's first tracking timestamp, 200 ms history, horizons 50/100/200 ms), what motion regime does the observed 200 ms future occupy on development participants, and how long does supplied ball tracking continue after the cutoff? This decides whether a gravity dynamics model is a physical candidate or a deliberately mismatched comparator before any real-data estimator run.

not_opened.P0004: historically consulted validation participant; not reopened for design decisions
not_opened.P0005: locked test participant; never opened by this packet

eligibility: unchanged baseline rule: run_prefix_forecast.fit_prefix and target_index (cutoff 2.0 s, history 0.2 s, >= 3 finite samples, no gap > 1.6 frames incl. window edges, first native target at or after each horizon within one frame)
units: metres and seconds; source feet converted by 0.3048; time re-zeroed to the first tracking timestamp

diagnostics.cutoff_state: height z and OLS velocity (fit_prefix) at the cutoff
diagnostics.future_fits: least-squares fits to finite ball samples in (cutoff, cutoff + 0.2 s], time relative to the cutoff: constant velocity (per-axis linear), gravity-only (fixed -g on z, linear otherwise), free quadratic; report 3D RMSE of each and the free-quadratic vertical acceleration 2*c2_z
diagnostics.tracking_tail: last finite ball sample time minus the cutoff
diagnostics.release_heuristic: wms.physics.free_throw.select_ballistic_window with its defaults over the WHOLE trajectory; a noncausal diagnostic only, never a label or model input. The reported time is the START of the selected gravity-consistent window, and equal fits are tie-broken toward later frames, so it marks where ballistic-looking motion is present, not the release instant. Timing is categorised relative to the history window and future window, or none_found

decision: report counts, reasons and quantiles (5/25/50/75/95) by session/participant and overall; no thresholds are applied; the next task card is frozen from these distributions
